8389670: C2: VectorBitwiseBlendNode assert when inputs are not vector Nodes

`VectorBitwiseBlendNode`'s constructor requires that all of its inputs
are vector nodes, but `Ideal_XorV_to_VectorBitwiseBlend` does not check
whether the matched inputs are vectors. As a result, the following
assert can be triggered in certain cases:

```
assert(vec_false->bottom_type()->isa_vect() != nullptr &&
       vec_true->bottom_type()->isa_vect() != nullptr &&
       sel->bottom_type()->isa_vect() != nullptr,
       "inputs must all be vectors")
```

This issue was found by `VectorExpressionFuzzer` with seed
`-6141810283007668497`.

In dead or unreachable code, node inputs can be `Top`. `Top` is a
unique shared node, so these identity checks can succeed spuriously
when both sides are `Top`. The IR graph looks like:

```
            XorV                 // outer
           /   \
         Top  AndV
              /  \
            Top  XorV            // inner
                 /  \
               Top   b

```
Here `a` and `sel` are `Top`, and `inner_xor->in(1)` is also `Top`.
Because `Top` is unique,`inner_xor->in(1) == a` succeeds, so
`Ideal_XorV_to_VectorBitwiseBlend` mistakenly matches and creates
`VectorBitwiseBlend(Top, b, Top)`

which then fails the "inputs must all be vectors" assert.

Normally, the inputs to VectorBitwiseBlendNode are vector nodes, the Top
node is the only exception. So this PR fixes the issue by checking that
`a`, `b`, and `sel`, if any of them is Top node, bail out of
the transform.
